title: Move authenticated-read proofs off the Board's ref read

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-430#move-authenticated-read-proofs-off-the-board-ref-read at bca2def1a3cccc0eef543e1f836a1452c345d445

Verdict: Caught. The fault is caught on the timed-out revision-check path and the owner-unavailable revision-check path. It is not caught on the HTTP 503 path that key example 1 names; see "Limit" below.

Promise (key example 1): when a fake gh answers the revision check (`&since=`) with HTTP 503, the read reports the "while reading main of" failure and records an incident in the `revision-check` category. I kept the suggested target. One finding narrowed it: the diagnostic history and the incident record take their category from the same entry, built in recordFailedRead (dashboard/server/readDiagnostics.ts). That entry is pushed to `failures` and passed to appendIncident. So one category fault reaches both.

Fault: in dashboard/server/readDiagnosticContext.ts, categoryOf mapped `case "revision-check": return "ref";` instead of `"revision-check"`. This is the pre-retarget category, so it is a plausible regression. No fixtures or assertions were changed.

Independent witness (a temporary scratch spec, deleted afterwards): a development-boundary server with its own machine directory; fake gh answers every call with HTTP 503; one checkedAt (`&since=`) read; then inspect() and incidentEntries(machine).
- Baseline: the response was 502 "GitHub answered HTTP 503 to the local GitHub CLI while reading main of terryyin/open-dough." with recovery "transient". It produced 2 diagnostics and 2 incident entries, all with category "revision-check" and status 503.
- Faulted: the response message was identical. It produced 2 diagnostics and 2 incident entries, all with category "ref" and status 503. The wrong behavior happened on the 503 path in both the diagnostic history and the incident record, while the message stayed correct.

Maintained checks examined, run with the focused commands in an isolated scratch worktree:
- dashboard/backend-tests/observation/authenticated-read-shared-listing-failures.spec.ts (3 tests).
  - Baseline: all 3 passed.
  - Faulted: the test "a 504 listing, a timed-out listing, and a rate-limited listing keep nothing; the next check asks again" failed at :108. That is the `expect.poll(() => inspect(timedOut)).toMatchObject({ failures: arrayContaining([objectContaining({ category: "revision-check", pin, cause: "timed-out" })]) })` assertion. The diff showed the received value as `"category": "ref"` with cause "timed-out". The other 2 tests were skipped because the file runs serially.
  - Restored: all 3 passed.
- e2e/observation/authenticated-read-owner-failures.spec.ts (6 tests).
  - Baseline: all 6 passed.
  - Faulted: all 6 failed at :89, the per-failure `toMatchObject({ cause: "owner-unavailable", ownerCause, category: "revision-check", source })`. The diff showed `"category": "ref"`. The loosened `failures.length > 0` check did not hide the fault: failures were recorded, and the loop checked the category of each one.
- Also checked by reading, without running: authenticated-read-transient-eligibility.spec.ts. It asserts the 503 `&since=` response message exactly, but it never inspects diagnostics or incidents. authenticated-read-incident-record.spec.ts and authenticated-read-diagnostics*.spec.ts assert incident and diagnostic content only for pinned reads, category "content".

Limit: the maintained catch is on the timed-out and owner-unavailable revision-check paths. It is not on the 503 path. No examined maintained check both drives a 503 revision check and asserts the category of the diagnostic or incident it records. No examined maintained check reads the persisted incident record for a revision-check failure. The persisted-incident side is covered only indirectly, because diagnostics and incidents share one entry. So a fault confined to 503 handling, such as an `http`-cause revision-check failure skipping recordFailedRead or getting a different category, would not be caught by the checks I examined. I did not inject that narrower fault, so this is unconfirmed.

Next proof action: none is required for the category-mapping fault. If the maintainer wants key example 1 proved literally, add one maintained assertion: after a 503 `&since=` read, inspect() or incidentEntries() shows a failed-read entry with category "revision-check" and status 503. The natural place is the eligibility or shared-listing-failures spec.

Prior disposition: this matches the story's own plan. The incident-record specs were moved to a pinned (`content`) read, and revision-check categories are asserted as diagnostics in shared-listing-failures and owner-failures. The probe confirms that those diagnostics assertions catch a category regression. It does not create a new repair decision.

Restoration: the faulted run used a trap that ran `git checkout -- dashboard/server/readDiagnosticContext.ts`. Afterwards the witness spec was deleted. The scratch checkout then had `git status --short` empty, HEAD bca2def1a3cc. The same commands passed again (3/3 backend, 6/6 e2e, outcomes from the proof records). The scratch worktree /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/d8dd9009/tmp/ic-scratch was removed with `git worktree remove --force` and then pruned. The probe logs and proof records in /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/d8dd9009/tmp/witness were deleted.

Costs:
- Test runtime: about 46 s, measured as wall-clock around each npm invocation (including npm and Playwright startup), over 6 runs. Backend: baseline 10 s (3 maintained tests plus the witness), fault 8 s, restore 3 s. E2E: baseline 11 s, fault 8 s, restore 6 s.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the check, and no separate measure exists.
- Agent effort: unavailable as tokens or time; no meter was exposed to this worker. Count: about 25 tool calls (counted from this session).

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 182577 ms (measured), from 1795738630000 to 1795738812577 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: bca2def1a3cccc0eef543e1f836a1452c345d445 — Caught — no follow-up (the next proof action needs no new or stronger proof).
